title: Baselines and metric honesty

protocol.name: year2022_2023
protocol.test: the whole 2023 window (report only — never fitted, never selected on)
protocol.model note: no model change: this stage fixes the *reporting* so every claim names the baseline it beats

gates.name: GATE: every window summary names its baselines
gates.target: persistence_1step, persistence_horizon_matched, clear_sky_naive (MAE + energy error), diurnal climatology
gates.observed: persistence at one step (15 min) and at the horizon, the clear-sky naive baseline with its energy error, and the training-hour climatology are all reported on every window

gates.name: GATE: the primary metrics are reported
gates.target: daylight % of rated, energy error, MAE/RMSE/bias, P10-P90 coverage, tribunal survival, rejection counts
gates.observed: the daylight MAE as a percentage of the rated DC power is 9.82 % (2022 validation); the energy error, MAE, RMSE, bias, coverage, survival and the rejection counts are reported next to it

gates.name: GATE: 'beats persistence' names which persistence
gates.observed: the model beats the *horizon-matched* persistence by 3.3x on the 2022 validation window (21,312 W vs 69,867 W) and by 4.0x on the 2023 window (17,260 W vs 68,866 W). The 15-minute persistence is reported separately (9,323 W on 2022 validation, 14,116 W on 2023) because it is scored on a single step and is therefore not comparable with a 96-step window MAE
gates.note: The two persistences are very different numbers, and an unqualified 'beats persistence' claim would be misleading either way.

allowed: The model beats the horizon-matched persistence by 3.3x (2022 validation) and 4.0x (2023), with the qualifier named.
The 15-minute persistence is reported on its own row, with the note that it is a single-step score.
The clear-sky naive baseline is reported with its MAE and its energy error.
The daylight error is reported as a percentage of the rated DC power.
forbidden: Any claim about the load, SOC or grid channels as validated skill.

notes: The baseline table is now per target and per model, so the solar and the load baselines can never be confused.
The clearance of the old 'persistence_origin' name: the horizon-matched persistence and the 15-minute persistence are separate rows.
